name: showreel-c3-terracotta-colour

voice.text: Was the Terracotta Army once painted in bright colours? In 1974, farmers digging a well in China struck a clay head. It was one of about 8,000 soldiers buried with the first emperor. Over 2,200 years ago, painters gave each one pink skin and bright robes. But the paint sat on lacquer, which shrinks in dry air. Within minutes of digging, the colour flakes away. Turns out, the grey army was dressed in colour.

caption:
The Terracotta Army was never meant to be grey. Over 2,200 years ago every soldier was painted: pink skin, robes of red, blue, green and purple, laid over a coat of lacquer. Out of the damp earth that lacquer dries, shrinks and curls, and the colour flakes off within minutes. 🎨

Send this to someone who has seen the warriors. Which landmark should we repaint next? 👇
